source_snapshot.title: fix(view): say when -p was not honoured, and show the URL in status
source_snapshot.body:
Follow-up to #358 (thanks @Hiro-Chiba), picking up the two pieces I flagged when closing #360.

## `-p` is still silently ignored

#358 fixed the real bug — the already-running branch printed an unreachable URL built from the port just requested. It reports the running port now, but says nothing about the request:

```
$ ix view -p 19124 start
[ok] Visualizer is already running (PID 65764)
  http://[redacted]19123
```

The URL is right. But you asked for 19124, got 19123, and nothing said so — you find out by noticing the number changed. Now:

```
[ok] Visualizer is already running (PID 65764)
  http://[redacted]19123
[!] You asked for port 19124, but it is serving on 19123.
    Run 'ix view stop' then 'ix view -p 19124' to move it.
```

Keyed on whether `-p` was **typed** (`getOptionValueSource("port") === "cli"`), not on whether it differs from 8080. Comparing against the default would stay silent for someone who explicitly passed `-p 8080` to a server running elsewhere — exactly the case they typed the flag to find out about — and would nag anyone who typed nothing.

## `status` can answer its own question now

The port is recorded as of #358, so:

```
$ ix view status
[ok] Visualizer is running (PID 65764)
  http://[redacted]19123
```

Silent rather than guessing for an instance old enough to have neither a port file nor a server script to recover one from — a confidently wrong URL is what #358 removed and this must not reintroduce it through the warning path.

## Tests

Extends #358's `view-running-port.test.ts` rather than adding a competing file: five more cases through their `runView` harness (mismatch warns, no-flag stays quiet, status shows the URL, status stays silent when unknown), plus three unit cases on the extracted `runningInstanceLines`.

Full suite green — 647 tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint src` clean.

commits.message:
fix(view): say when -p was not honoured, and show the URL in status

Follow-up to #358, which stopped the already-running branch printing an
unreachable URL built from the port just requested. It reports the real
port now, but says nothing about the request, so `ix view -p 19124`
against a server on 19123 prints a correct URL for a port nobody asked
for and never mentions the flag was ignored — you find out by noticing
the number changed.

Warns on the mismatch instead, keyed on whether -p was typed rather than
whether it differs from 8080: comparing against the default would stay
silent for someone who explicitly passed `-p 8080` to a server running
elsewhere, which is the case they typed the flag to find out about, and
would nag anyone who typed nothing at all.

`ix view status` also prints the URL now. The port is recorded as of
#358, so status can finally answer the question people run it to ask. It
stays silent rather than guessing for an instance old enough to have
neither a port file nor a server script to recover one from.

The decision is pulled out as a pure function — inline in the command
action it could only be exercised by launching a detached server.

fix(view): say the port is unknown from status, not nothing

Review follow-up. `ix view` and `ix view status` disagreed in exactly the
state that motivated #358: with a live PID but no recoverable port, `ix view`
printed the "port is unknown" advisory and told you how to recover, while
`status` printed the PID line and stopped.

Neither guessed a URL, so this was never a #358 regression -- but silence is
the wrong answer for someone who ran `status` *for* the URL, and it was also
unpinned: the existing test only asserted the absence of "http://localhost",
which the advisory satisfies too, so the behaviour could drift either way.

Route status through runningInstanceLines so the two branches cannot drift.
`status` takes no -p, so the mismatch branch is unreachable from here.

Confirmed non-vacuous: with the old two-line form restored, the new test fails
on "expected '[ok] Visualizer is running (PID 4242)' to contain 'unknown'".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PZhcNcCtFQ6Bz2XMDpJPJS

reviews.body:
Extracting `runningInstanceLines` as a pure function is the right move — inline in the command action this branch could only be exercised by launching a detached server, which is why the gap survived #358 in the first place.

`getOptionValueSource("port") === "cli"` is the correct predicate, and the comment explains why the obvious alternative is wrong in *both* directions: comparing against the default stays silent for someone who explicitly typed `-p 8080` against a server running elsewhere (exactly the case they typed the flag to discover), and nags anyone who typed nothing.

The `runningPort === null` test earns its place — asserting that no `http://localhost` appears at all is a direct regression guard on the confidently-wrong URL #358 removed. Easy to reintroduce that through a new warning path; now it fails loudly.

`status` reporting the URL is the small one that will get used the most.

All checks green. Approving.

Two independent review passes (one on your commit, one on my follow-up). Merging.

**Your `getOptionValueSource` approach checks out empirically, not just by reading.** Against the installed commander 15.0.0 source: `.default()` stamps `'default'` (`command.js:679`), the argv path stamps `'cli'` (`:713`), and `'env'` is only registered when `[redacted]()` is used (`:719`) — which this isn't. 12 argv orderings probed, and every genuinely typed `-p` returns `cli`, including `--port=19124`, `-p19124`, `-p` after the subcommand, and the `-p 8080` case your comment calls out. `main.ts` does no argv rewriting and no config layer supplies a port, so the source is only ever `cli` or `default`. The warning cannot silently never fire.

**The wiring is genuinely tested**, which was my main worry given the extracted-pure-function shape. `runView` builds a real `new Command()`, calls the production `registerViewCommand`, and parses real argv — nothing stubs commander or the option source. Forcing the source comparison to fail breaks a test:
`× says the requested port was not honoured — expected '[ok] Visualizer is already running (P…' to contain 'You asked for port 19124'`
All five load-bearing lines mutation-checked; each kills exactly the test that claims it.

**I pushed one commit.** `ix view` and `ix view status` disagreed in precisely the state that motivated #358: with a live PID and no recoverable port, `ix view` printed the advisory and a recovery command, `status` printed the PID line and stopped. Not a #358 regression — neither guesses a URL, and `readRunningPort` funnels everything through `parsePort`, so a corrupt port file yields `null`, never a bad port. But silence is the wrong answer for someone who ran `status` *for* the URL, and it was unpinned: the old assertion was only `not.toContain("http://localhost")`, which the advisory satisfies too, so it could have drifted either way.

`status` now routes through `runningInstanceLines` so the two branches cannot drift. It takes no `-p`, so the mismatch branch is unreachable from there — `portWasRequested: false` means the `0` is never read, confirmed against every reachable `runningPort` value. The old assertion is retained, not replaced. Bug restored: `× says the port is unknown from status instead of printing nothing`, exactly one failure, so nothing else depended on the silence.

One cosmetic thing I left alone: when the port and scope advisories both fire, they print two recovery commands that each silently undo the other's intent (one drops `--all`, the other drops `-p`). Uncommon state, and worth a follow-up rather than widening this PR.
